transformations.edit: Replaced the seed-only contract/body string recorder with an executable Verus target function, adapting the inherent `[T]` receiver to an explicit `slice: &mut [T]` argument and naming the return.
Attached the generated mutable pointer-range postconditions directly to the executable target: `slice_mut_ptr_range_starts_at_slice(old(slice)@, range)` and `final(slice)@ == old(slice)@`.
Preserved the Rust 1.96 target flow: `let start = self.as_mut_ptr();`, `let end = unsafe { start.add(self.len()) };`, and `start..end`; the implicit receiver is the only source syntax adaptation.

Reused the already verified `core::slice::as_mut_ptr` dependency shape through a local executable `as_mut_ptr` wrapper with `slice_start_mut_ptr`, and isolated only the unsafe raw-pointer `start.add(self.len())` end computation as a named source-backed provenance/range boundary.
